advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the deciding_digest for the 'cycle' reason cover the transitive blocks-graph the cycle check reads, or exclude the cycle reason from digest-based skipping so it re-attempts when the graph changes.
evidence: impossible_links.py:129 `if depth == 0:` — deps are captured only for the endpoint itself, not the transitive graph
_graph.py:127 `def _get_all_blocked_by(ticket_id, tracker_dir)` does a BFS over `state.get("deps")` of many tickets, so cycle verdicts depend on intermediate tickets not in the fingerprint
_links.py:229 `if check_would_create_cycle(...)` raises the cycle verdict from that transitive check
advisory.finding: The deciding_digest fingerprint only captures each endpoint's own status, parent chain, and direct deps, but a 'cycle' verdict is decided by a transitive traversal of the entire blocks-graph (_get_all_blocked_by). Breaking the offending edge on an intermediate ticket (neither source nor target) makes the link creatable without changing either endpoint's fingerprint, so the digest still matches and the link is skipped forever.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile should_skip's per-skip dirtying with the 'zero writes on a converged pass' docstring — either don't mark dirty for pure metadata updates or correct the docstring.
evidence: impossible_links.py:172 docstring: 'writes only when something actually changed, so a converged pass touches the file zero times'
impossible_links.py:234 `record["last_seen"] = time.time()` / :236 `self._dirty = True` inside should_skip on every matched skip
advisory.finding: ImpossibleLinkStore.should_skip() mutates last_seen/skips and sets self._dirty = True on every skip, so any steady-state pass with recorded impossible links rewrites the JSON file every pass. This contradicts the class docstring claim that 'a converged pass touches the file zero times'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish target-closed from source-closed in classify (or rename the reason) so the recorded reason is not misleading for depends_on target-closed failures.
evidence: impossible_links.py:79 `(REASON_CLOSED_SOURCE, ("cannot create", "is closed"))` also matches the target-closed message
_links.py:270 `f"cannot create depends_on link — target ticket '{target_id}' is closed"`
advisory.finding: A target-closed failure for a depends_on link ('cannot create depends_on link — target ticket ... is closed') is classified as REASON_CLOSED_SOURCE, mislabelling the recorded reason as source-closed when it is the target that is closed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end skip-oracle test for the redundant_ancestry and cycle verdicts (build a real ancestor-descendant / cycle-forming graph, assert pass 2 attempts zero writes and the store records the correct reason).
evidence: Only the `store` fixture (closed source) drives the full loop: `test_impossible_link_is_attempted_once_then_never_again`, `test_the_skip_is_recorded_durably_...` and friends all use `store` which does `rebar.transition(a, "open", "closed", ...)` producing only the closed_source verdict.

classify tests cover all three: `(_CLOSED_SOURCE, "closed_source"), (_REDUNDANT, "redundant_ancestry"), (_CYCLE, "cycle")` — but ABSENCE: no test constructs a real ancestor-descendant or cycle-forming graph and asserts the second pass skips the write.
Commit lists three permanent reasons; only one has an integration-level regression guard.
advisory.finding: The end-to-end two-pass skip oracle only exercises the closed_source reason; the redundant_ancestry and cycle verdicts — two of the three permanent shapes the feature memoizes — are only tested at the classify() string level and never driven through record()/should_skip() against a real add_dependency failure. A regression in the skip/record path specific to those two shapes (e.g. a digest or key mismatch that only manifests for hierarchy/cycle endpoints) would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that reparents an endpoint (and/or changes its dep set) and asserts the recorded impossible link is re-qualified for a fresh attempt, so ancestry/deps digest invalidation has a regression guard.
evidence: _endpoint_fingerprint builds `parts.append("ancestry=" + ">".join(chain))` and `parts.append("deps=" + deps_repr)` as digest inputs.
`test_a_comment_on_an_endpoint_does_not_requalify_the_link` covers a NON-structural edit but not a structural ancestry/deps change.
ABSENCE: no test reparents an endpoint or alters its dep set and asserts the link is re-qualified for one attempt.
advisory.finding: deciding_digest / _endpoint_fingerprint include the endpoint parent chain (ancestry) and dep set as invalidation inputs, but only a status change (reopen) is tested for re-qualification. Reparenting an endpoint or changing its dep set — explicitly claimed in the commit message as a re-qualification trigger ('reparenting an endpoint re-qualifies the link') — has no test, so a regression dropping ancestry or deps from the fingerprint would still pass every existing test.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 385 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug b8b1-6462-b4f1-4a1d has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan b8b1-6462-b4f1-4a1d` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review b8b1-6462-b4f1-4a1d` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan b8b1-6462-b4f1-4a1d --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
